facts.statement: Coronosaurus lived during the middle Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Coronosaurus is a genus of centrosaurine ceratopsian dinosaurs which lived in the Late Cretaceous, in the middle Campanian stage.

facts.statement: Phillip J. Currie discovered the remains of Coronosaurus in two bone beds within the Oldman Formation of Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: Its remains, two bone beds, were discovered by Phillip J. Currie in the Oldman Formation of Alberta, Canada

facts.statement: The fossils of Coronosaurus come from two bone beds excavated by Philip Currie between 1996 and 2000.
facts.quote: Coronosaurus is known from two bone beds, BB 138 and MRR BB, located in the upper unit of the Oldman Formation, of the Belly River Group, excavated by Philip Currie between 1996 and 2000.

facts.statement: Michael J. Ryan and Anthony P. Russell originally described the type species as Centrosaurus brinkmani in 2005.
facts.quote: Michael J. Ryan and Anthony P. Russell described and named the type species, then as Centrosaurus brinkmani, in 2005.

facts.statement: Ryan, Evans, and Shepherd established the separate genus Coronosaurus in 2012 after phylogenetic studies showed the species did not belong with Centrosaurus apertus.
facts.quote: Later studies, however, did not recover a monophyletic clade with the genus' type species Centrosaurus apertus in phylogenetic analyses. Due to this, Ryan, David C. Evans and Kieran M. Shepherd erected the genus Coronosaurus for the species in 2012.

facts.statement: Coronosaurus possessed a large frill, brow horns, a nasal horn, and unique irregular spiky bone masses on its frill.
facts.quote: Like other ceratopsids, Coronosaurus had a large frill and horns on its head. These include a small pair of brow horns over its eyes, a large nasal horn on its snout, and, unique among ceratopsians, irregular, spiky bone masses on its frill.

facts.statement: Coronosaurus grew to be around 5 meters long and weighed approximately 2 tonnes.
facts.quote: Growing up to around 5 m long and 2 t in weight, it was mid-sized for its kind.

facts.statement: The genus name Coronosaurus is derived from Latin and Greek words meaning "crown" and "lizard," referencing the crown-like appearance of extra bone plates on its skull.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the Latin corona, meaning "crown" in reference to the multiple occurrences of extra epiparietals that cover the posterior margin of its parietal, giving it a crown-like appearance, and saurus (Latinized from Greek sauros), meaning "lizard".

facts.statement: The describer Michael Ryan stated that the name Coronosaurus was inspired by the sun's corona due to the dinosaur's frill ornamentation.
facts.quote: In 2020, in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, Ryan was asked about the naming of the dinosaur, and stated he came up with it because its frill ornamentation made him think of the corona of the sun.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated in 2010 that Coronosaurus reached a body length of 5 meters and a weight of 2 tonnes.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul in 2010 estimated its body length at 5 m and its weight at 2 t.

facts.statement: Coronosaurus uniquely possesses accessory epiparietal ossifications that fuse to the rear and top of its skull frill.
facts.quote: Uniquely among ceratopsians, Coronosaurus possesses a number of accessory epiparietal ossifications rear parietal frill of the skull that fuse to the posterior and dorsal frill surface.

facts.statement: The unique bone masses on the frill of Coronosaurus develop from short spines that fuse together as the individual grows.
facts.quote: They develop through ontogeny, the growth of the individual, as short spines that may fuse along their adjacent margins into larger, irregular bone masses.

facts.statement: Adult Coronosaurus had inflated brow horns that did not project laterally over the eye sockets like those of other ceratopsians.
facts.quote: It had as an adult inflated supraorbital horncores — the "brow horns" above the eye sockets — but not elongated as in Zuniceratops, chasmosaurines, and more basal centrosaurines (like Albertaceratops and Diabloceratops), that project laterally (to the sides) over the orbit.

facts.statement: Coronosaurus is classified as a member of the Centrosaurini subgroup of centrosaurines.
facts.quote: The genus is classified as a member of the Centrosaurini, a group of derived centrosaurines which has also been found include taxa such as Styracosaurus, Spinops, Rubeosaurus, and Centrosaurus, the genus it was originally placed within.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis identified Coronosaurus as the sister taxon to Styracosaurus, placing it in a more advanced position than Centrosaurus apertus.
facts.quote: In the resultant tree, it was found to be in more advanced position than Spinops and C. apertus, as the sister taxon of Styracosaurus. Thus the new generic name, Coronosaurus, was given to it.

facts.statement: Studies suggest that the environment where Coronosaurus lived was an ancient coastal plain.
facts.quote: Studies suggest that the paleoenvironment of the Oldman Formation was an ancient coastal plain.

facts.statement: The Oldman Formation, where Coronosaurus fossils were found, also contains remains of various theropods, ceratopsids, hadrosaurids, and ankylosaurids.
facts.quote: In addition to remains of Coronosaurus, this formation has produced the remains of the theropods Saurornitholestes, Daspletosaurus, Troodon, Dromaeosaurus and Hesperonychus, the ceratopsids Albertaceratops, Chasmosaurus, and Anchiceratops, the hadrosaurids Brachylophosaurus, Gryposaurus, Parasaurolophus, and Corythosaurus, the thescelosaurid Albertadromeus and the ankylosaurid Scolosaurus.

facts.statement: Coronosaurus belongs to the family Ceratopsidae.
facts.quote: familia: Ceratopsidae

facts.statement: Coronosaurus is classified within the subfamily Centrosaurinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Centrosaurinae

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated in 2010 that the body length of Coronosaurus was 5 meters and its weight was two tonnes.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul en 2010 estimó su longitud del cuerpo en 5 metros, su peso en dos toneladas.

facts.statement: Adult Coronosaurus possessed large supraorbital spines, or "frontal horns," above the eye sockets that were not elongated laterally like those in Zuniceratops or basal centrosaurines such as Albertaceratops and Diabloceratops.
facts.quote: Tenía una especie de espinas supraorbitales grandes en losadultos, los "cuernos de la frente", sobre las cuencas de los ojos, pero no alargadas como en Zuniceratops, chasmosaurínidos y centrosaurínidos basales como Albertaceratops y Diabloceratops, que se proyectan lateralmente sobre la órbita.

facts.statement: Coronosaurus is unique among ceratopsids for possessing accessory epiparietal ossifications on the posterior parietal bar that fuse with the posterior and dorsal edge surfaces.
facts.quote: El Coronosaurus es único entre los ceratopsidos ya que posee en la parte posterior del cráneo una cantidad de osificaciones epipáreas accesorias en su barra parietal posterior que se fusionan a las superficies del borde posterior y dorsal.

facts.statement: The type species, originally named Centrosaurus brinkmani, was first described and named by Michael J. Ryan and Anthony P. Russell in 2005 as a new species of the genus Centrosaurus.
facts.quote: La especie tipo de Coronosaurus, Centrosaurus brinkmani , fue descrita por primera vez y nombrada por Michael J. Ryan y Anthony P. Russell en 2005 como una nueva especie del género Centrosaurus.

facts.statement: Michael J. Ryan, David C. Evans, and Kieran M. Shepherd erected the genus Coronosaurus for C. brinkmani in 2012 because C. apertus and C. brinkmani did not form a monophyletic clade in recent phylogenetic analyses.
facts.quote: Michael J. Ryan, David C. Evans y Kieran M. Shepherd posteriormente erigieron el género Coronosaurus para C. brinkmani en 2012, ya que Centrosaurus apertus y C. brinkmani no formaron un clado monofilético en varios análisis filogenéticos recientes.

facts.statement: Coronosaurus is known from two bone beds located in the upper unit of the Oldman Formation, part of the Belly River Group.
facts.quote: Coronosaurus es conocido a partir de dos lechos óseos ubicados en la unidad superior de la Formación Oldman , del Grupo del Río Belly.

facts.statement: Most, if not all, of the ceratopsian material from bone bed BB 138 in Dinosaur Provincial Park, Alberta, and the MRR BB near Warner, Alberta, has been referred to C. brinkmani.
facts.quote: La mayor parte del material de ceratópsido, si no todos, de BB 138 en Dinosaur Provincial Park , Alberta , y el MRR BB cerca de Warner, Alberta, se remitió a C. brinkmani.

facts.statement: The holotype of Coronosaurus is TMP 2002.68.1., a large adult-sized parietal with an almost complete midline bar and a partial posterior bar with the left epiparietal processes 1 and 3 and the right epiparietal processes 1 and 2 partially eroded.
facts.quote: El holotipo de Coronosaurus es TMP 2002.68.1., un parietal grande del tamaño de un adulto con una barra de línea media casi completa y una barra posterior parcial con los procesos epiparietales 1 y 3 izquierdos y procesos epiparietales 1 y 2 derecha parcialmente erosionados.

facts.statement: In the phylogenetic tree, Coronosaurus was found in a more advanced position than Spinops and C. apertus, being a sister taxon to Styracosaurus, which led to it being given the new generic name Coronosaurus.
facts.quote: En el esquema de árbol fue encontrado en una posición más avanzada que Spinops y C. apertus, siendo un taxón hermano con Styracosaurus. De ahí que a este taxón se le diera un nuevo nombre genérico, Coronosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2016, Ryan et al. placed Coronosaurus as a sister taxon to a clade formed by Centrosaurus and Spinops, separate from Styracosaurus and Rubeosaurus, all within Centrosaurini.
facts.quote: En 2016 Ryan et al. en su descripción del cráneo parcial CMN 8804 como un Nasutoceratopsini colocó a Coronosaurus hermano a un clado formado por Centrosaurus y Spinops, separado de Styracosaurus y Rubeosaurus todos dentro de Centrosaurini.

facts.statement: Studies suggest that the paleoenvironment of the Oldman Formation was an ancient coastal plain.
facts.quote: Los estudios sugieren que el paleoambiente de la Formación Oldman era una antigua llanura costera.

facts.statement: Besides Coronosaurus remains, the Oldman Formation has yielded fossils of theropods like Saurornitholestes and Daspletosaurus, ceratopsids like Albertaceratops and Chasmosaurus, hadrosaurids like Brachylophosaurus and Gryposaurus, the ornithopod Albertadromeus, and the ankylosaurid Scolosaurus.
facts.quote: Además de los restos de Coronosaurus, esta formación ha producido los restos de los terópodos Saurornitholestes, Daspletosaurus, Troodon, Dromaeosaurus y Hesperonychus, los ceratopsidos Albertaceratops, Chasmosaurus y Anchiceratops, los hadrosáuridos Brachylophosaurus, Gryposaurus, Parasaurolophusy Corythosaurus, el ornitópodo Albertadromeus y el anquilosáurido Scolosaurus.

facts.statement: The time range for Coronosaurus is the Campanian stage, spanning from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Coronosaurus belongs to the parent group Centrosaurini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Centrosaurini

facts.statement: Coronosaurus is classified in the family Ceratopsidae.
facts.quote: Family: Ceratopsidae

facts.statement: Coronosaurus is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Coronosaurus possesses a unique epiparietal 3 that develops variably as a short tongue-shaped hook or a conical tip oriented dorsolaterally, following the curve of the frill.
facts.quote: Coronosaurus tiene también un epiparietal 3 de forma única. Se desarrolla de forma variable como un gancho corto con forma de lengua o una punta cónica que se orienta dorsolateralmente, siguiendo la curva del volante.

facts.statement: As a subadult, the postorbital horns of Coronosaurus are pyramidal in shape with a slight lateral flexion in the distal upper half.
facts.quote: Como subadulto, sus cornamentas postorbitales tienen forma piramidal con una ligera inflexión lateral en la mitad distal, superior.

facts.statement: The core of the Coronosaurus nasal horn is erect and laterally compressed, with a blunt tip formed by the fusion of opposing nasals.
facts.quote: Su núcleo de cuerno nasal erecto y comprimido lateralmente tiene una punta roma que se forma a partir de la fusión de los nasales opuestas.
